findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the exact full-replication trigger mechanism and reconcile it with the disabled remote-plugin-admin precondition (setup-replication.sh: ALLOW_REMOTE_RELOAD default 0; replicateOnStartup=false), e.g. state that the trigger uses admin SSH `replication start --all --remote github --now --wait` with ALLOW_REMOTE_RELOAD=1, or specify the operator-run on-box path.
evidence: Plan: 'Trigger full replication for remote `github`; this trigger/backfill is the mechanism that creates any missing refs'
infra/gerrit/setup-replication.sh:14 'REMOTE PLUGIN ADMIN IS DISABLED on this instance'; lines 101-117 gate `plugin reload`/admin SSH behind ALLOW_REMOTE_RELOAD (default 0)
infra/gerrit/replication.config:53 `replicateOnStartup = false` — a restart does not auto-trigger a full sweep
infra/gerrit/setup-replication.sh:52 documents the trigger form `replication start --all --remote github --now --wait` (runs over admin SSH)
findings.finding: The plan's 'Trigger full replication for remote github' step is the load-bearing external capability (the AC requires 'full replication has been triggered successfully'), but it names no mechanism and does not reconcile the disabled-remote-admin precondition the repo documents. The repo's setup-replication.sh states REMOTE PLUGIN ADMIN IS DISABLED on this instance (ALLOW_REMOTE_RELOAD default 0) and replication.config sets replicateOnStartup=false, so a restart alone will not replicate; the documented trigger form `replication start --all --remote github --now --wait` runs over admin SSH, which is the disabled capability. Whether the trigger is achievable as described is therefore UNVERIFIED.
findings.location: Plan > 'Trigger full replication for remote github'; AC line 'The live Gerrit host has the updated replication config applied and full replication has been triggered successfully.'
scenarios: Operator applies the config and restarts Gerrit but no full-replication sweep runs because replicateOnStartup=false and the SSH trigger requires admin plugin access that is disabled by default
The change-ref namespace never converges on the mirror, so the 'refs/changes/* visibility' AC cannot be met despite the config being correct
findings.suggested_fix: Update the trigger step to cite the repo-documented command `replication start --all --remote github --now --wait` and note it requires enabling admin SSH (ALLOW_REMOTE_RELOAD=1) since remote plugin admin is disabled by default and replicateOnStartup=false means a restart will not backfill on its own.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the RETIRE/cleanup disposition for the mirrored `refs/changes/*` namespace: whether abandoned/obsolete change refs are ever pruned on the GitHub mirror, who owns that, or an explicit accepted-growth rationale.
evidence: Plan replicates `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*` to the org-private GitHub mirror with no statement of how abandoned/merged change refs are pruned or retired on the mirror.

T9 checklist: 'There is a RETIRE/cleanup path — it doesn't leak/accumulate.' — the plan covers CREATE (replication trigger), UPDATE (full sweep convergence), and CONSUME (mirror-first action) but is silent on RETIRE.
findings.finding: The plan publishes and force-converges an ever-growing `refs/changes/*` namespace on the GitHub mirror but defines no RETIRE/cleanup path for those accumulated patchset refs; the shared mirrored state grows unbounded as changes accumulate over time.
findings.location: Plan step: 'Update only the Gerrit change-ref replication spec to the operator-approved forced refspec `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*`' and 'Trigger full replication for remote `github`'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that forcing `+refs/changes/*` addresses only Gerrit-side change-ref REWRITE/divergence convergence, and that the full-replication trigger (not the `+`) is what backfills the missing/lagging ref that caused Run 34235734839's 502 — so the two changes are not conflated as one fix.
evidence: infra/gerrit/replication.config:63: `push = refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*` — the change-ref refspec already exists (non-forced)
Plan (Operator ruling): 'The force applies to patchset refs and refs/changes/NN/NNNN/meta; it is not what creates a missing ref'
Plan bullet: 'Trigger full replication for remote github; this trigger/backfill is the mechanism that creates any missing refs, while the forced refspec is the operator-approved convergence behavior'
config comment lines 33-34/61-62: replication lag/misses are expected-by-design and covered by the checkout-gerrit-change-action gerrit-url fallback
findings.finding: The plan's headline config change (forcing `refs/changes/*` with a leading `+`) does not address the diagnosed root cause. The change-ref refspec is already present and non-forced (infra/gerrit/replication.config:63); the incident was a MISSING/lagging ref at validation time, and the plan itself concedes 'The force applies to patchset refs... it is not what creates a missing ref.' The load-bearing remedy is the separate 'Trigger full replication' step, not the `+`. The plan should make this separation explicit so an implementer does not believe flipping to `+` resolves the 502/lag incident.
scenarios: An implementer treats the `+` refspec as the incident fix and skips or under-executes the full-replication trigger, leaving missing change refs unconverged
A future reader assumes forcing prevents the 502 fallback, when only actual replication of the missing ref does

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the FORCED `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*` against the established NON-force one-way-door prior art (ADR-0010/ADR-0021) and the RCA: state explicitly why force is required when the diagnosed cause is a missing/lagging ref fixed by full-replication trigger, or drop the `+` and keep the non-force refspec plus the replication sweep.
evidence: ADR-0010: NON-force refspecs are described as 'the core safety property' and 'GitHub can never diverge silently'
docs/adr/0021-replication-change-refs.md line 19: 'push = refs/changes/*:refs/changes/* (non-force, no leading +, mirror = false)' — the established prior art is explicitly NON-force
Plan concedes: 'it is not what creates a missing ref' — yet the RCA is a missing ref, so the force does not address the diagnosed cause
Web (Gerrit replication docs / `replication start --all`): a missing ref is backfilled by triggering full replication, which the plan already includes as a separate step
The plan's own separate bullet triggers full replication as 'the mechanism that creates any missing refs' — making the added force orthogonal to the RCA
findings.finding: The plan adopts a FORCED refspec (`+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*`) that deviates from the established, ADR-documented NON-force one-way-door contract (ADR-0010 'core safety property', ADR-0021), without reconciling that novelty against the diagnosed root cause (a MISSING/lagging ref). Prior art in-repo and in Gerrit docs shows a missing ref is created by triggering full replication (`replication start --all`), not by adding force; patchset refs are append-only so force is not the fix. The plan should justify the force against this prior art or drop it.
findings.location: Operator ruling + Plan bullet 2 ('Update only the Gerrit change-ref replication spec to the operator-approved forced refspec `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*`')
scenarios: Reviewer/operator asks why the one-way-door non-force contract (ADR-0010/0021) is being weakened when the incident was a replication-lag/missing-ref, not a diverged/rewritten ref
A future force-push on the change namespace masks a real Gerrit-side history rewrite that the non-force refspec would have surfaced as a REJECTED_NONFASTFORWARD alarm
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) drop the leading `+` and rely on the full-replication trigger (`replication start --all`) to backfill the missing change ref, keeping the ADR-0010/0021 non-force contract intact; or (b) if force is genuinely wanted for change-metadata rewrites, add an ADR amendment that cites the prior-art non-force decision and justifies the scoped exception for the `refs/changes/*` namespace only.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the failure handling for the replication trigger: what constitutes a failed/partial run, the retry/re-trigger action, and how errors are surfaced before relying on the downstream Mirror Guard check.
evidence: 'Monitor replication output/disk/CPU enough to catch obvious initial-load failures' — vague, no failure action or retry defined
No described handling if the initial full-replication load errors, stalls, or partially completes
findings.finding: The replication trigger is an external/stateful operation, but its error handling is specified only as monitoring 'enough to catch obvious initial-load failures' with no defined action on failure, no timeout/retry, and no surfaced error state beyond the downstream Mirror Guard check.
findings.location: Plan steps 'Trigger full replication for remote github' and 'Monitor replication output/disk/CPU enough to catch obvious initial-load failures'
scenarios: The full-replication initial load stalls or errors on a subset of change refs; the operator has no defined next step until the later Mirror Guard run surfaces a lag alarm

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound and (if needed) throttle the initial `refs/changes/*` full-replication sweep: state the expected ref count/duration and how a stalled load is distinguished from a slow one, rather than only watching for obvious failures.
evidence: Plan says 'Trigger full replication for remote github; this trigger/backfill is the mechanism that creates any missing refs.'

`refs/changes/*` for a long-lived project can be a very large namespace (every patchset of every change), yet the plan only 'monitor[s] ... enough to catch obvious initial-load failures' without any throttle/batch or scale estimate.
ABSENCE: no expected-ref-count / duration / throttle bound is stated, so an operator cannot distinguish a slow-but-healthy initial load from a stalled one.
findings.finding: The full-replication backfill of `refs/changes/*` is not batched/throttled and its scale is not bounded, while T11 asks large backfills to be batched rather than run as one giant sweep.
findings.location: Plan > 'Trigger full replication for remote `github`' and 'Monitor replication output/disk/CPU enough to catch obvious initial-load failures.'
scenarios: The initial full-replication sweep pushes tens of thousands of change refs, saturating disk/CPU or the events queue and delaying convergence past the next Mirror Guard run.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a back-out assertion on the GitHub-side `refs/changes/*` state (not just config restoration), noting the force-push is a one-way transformation of the mirror and stating how convergence is confirmed or compensated-forward after any revert.
evidence: Operator ruling: 'The force applies to patchset refs and refs/changes/NN/NNNN/meta' and 'ensures the full replication sweep converges the mirrored change namespace even if Gerrit rewrites change metadata.'
The snapshot only preserves/reverts the config; reverting the config does NOT restore any GitHub change ref that the forced push already overwrote or rewound.
T11 post-rollback clause: a one-way transformation with no back-out must assert on state AFTER rollback, not merely that rollback completed.
findings.finding: The plan provides a config-level back-out (snapshot of `replication.config`) but does not assert on the AFTER-ROLLBACK state of the GitHub-side `refs/changes/*` refs, even though the forced refspec is a one-way transformation the operator ruling says will overwrite/converge the mirrored change namespace.
findings.location: Plan > 'Apply the repository config ... snapshotting the live replication.config first' and Operator ruling ('the full replication sweep converges the mirrored change namespace even if Gerrit rewrites change metadata').
scenarios: A forced replication rewinds or overwrites a `refs/changes/NN/.../meta` or patchset ref on GitHub that a concurrent CI checkout relies on; reverting replication.config afterward leaves the mirror's change refs in the force-pushed state with no compensating restore.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit back-out step for the operational force-push: on replication failure, restore the snapshotted replication.config and re-trigger from Gerrit (change refs are Gerrit-authoritative and re-derivable), and state this reversibility in the plan.
evidence: Operator ruling accepts force `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*` as a trade-off, and the plan snapshots replication.config first — but only the config is reversible per the plan
T4 remedy requires an explicit rollback/back-out, not just acknowledgement
Force applies to 'patchset refs and refs/changes/NN/NNNN/meta' — a partial/errant replication run has no described recovery
findings.finding: The plan force-publishes the change-ref namespace to the GitHub mirror (an explicitly accepted destructive trade-off) and snapshots the live replication.config for config rollback, but states no back-out path for the operational force-push itself if replication errors or corrupts the mirrored change namespace mid-run.
findings.location: Plan step 'Apply the repository config...' / 'Trigger full replication...' and Acceptance Criteria (host apply / full replication triggered)
scenarios: Full replication trigger fails partway or the force-push writes bad refs to the mirror and an operator needs to reverse it
findings.suggested_fix: Note that Gerrit remains the source of truth for refs/changes/*, so back-out = restore the config snapshot and re-run full replication; document this as the recovery path.
